properties.name: Rancho Acalanes (Elam Brown purchase)
properties.description: 3,329-acre Mexican land grant (granted 1834 to Candelario Valencia) bought by Elam Brown for $900 in 1847. It covers almost all of present-day Lafayette. Point is the city centroid, not a building.
properties.coord_source: area symbol at Nominatim city centroid

properties.name: Elam Brown's first home (Happy Valley area)
properties.description: Brown moved into the Happy Valley area Feb 7, 1848. His first permanent home was a pre-cut redwood frame house about two miles north of Lafayette. Exact site unknown.

properties.name: Brown's grist mill
properties.description: Grist mill on Lafayette Creek at Golden Gate Way near First St. It pulled the village centre toward Mt Diablo Blvd/Moraga Rd in the early 1860s.
properties.coord_source: estimated: Golden Gate Way near First St from OSM street geometry

properties.name: Milo Hough's Hotel
properties.description: First of three hotels near the Plaza. Later sold to Benjamin Shreve.

properties.name: Plaza (Elam Brown's gift)
properties.description: 100x150 ft triangle deeded to the town Nov 19, 1864. By the early 1860s it was ringed by the mill, a store, a school, a blacksmith and a hotel.

properties.name: Pioneer Store (Shreve's store & post office)
properties.description: Benjamin Shreve's store, post office and insurance agency, opened at this site in the early 1860s. Bought by Robert Elam McNeil in 1902. Still standing, remodeled with a false front.
properties.coord_source: US Census geocoder (matched Plaza Dr, verify)

properties.name: Lafayette Cemetery
properties.description: 4.5-acre hillside bought for $100 by the Cemetery Corporation, chaired by Elam Brown, in 1874.

properties.name: Hotel corner (Hastings / Lamp hotels)
properties.description: Mt Diablo Blvd & Moraga Rd. Norman Hastings' hotel burned in 1892, and Phillip Lamp's hotel, also on this corner, burned in 1925. No hotels were built here after that.

properties.name: Wayside Inn
properties.description: Two-story hotel and tavern built by Edward J. Brady in 1894 for cattle drovers. Bought by Pat Medau in 1921 and used as an ice cream parlor from 1925.
properties.coord_source: US Census geocoder 3521 Golden Gate Way

properties.name: Post office (Carrie Van Meter)
properties.description: Post office on Mt Diablo Blvd. Postmistress Carrie Van Meter (1904-27) also lent its 60 books, making her the first librarian. Exact site unknown.

properties.name: Town Hall
properties.description: Built 1914 by volunteers and the Lafayette Improvement Association. Dances here ran late enough that a special 3 AM train took partygoers home.

properties.name: West Lafayette station (Sacramento Northern)
properties.description: Electric interurban station at the end of School St, near Paradise Ct. Service through Lafayette began in 1913, passenger service ended in 1941 and freight in 1957.
properties.coord_source: estimated: east end of School St (OSM)

properties.name: Cornfield (future La Fiesta Shopping Center)
properties.description: Before 1915 a cornfield grew below Mt Diablo Blvd along Moraga Rd.
properties.coord_source: GAP: La Fiesta Square not geolocated

properties.name: Lafayette United Methodist Church (1893 school building)
properties.description: The congregation moved in 1927 into the former 1893 third school building.

properties.name: Lafayette Reservoir dam & outlet tower
properties.description: George Pollock Co. contract, July 1927. A slide in Sept 1928 forced a lower, wider redesign, and the dam was completed in 1933.

properties.name: Starks' Lafayette Meat Market
properties.description: Moved in 1920 to the SE corner of Mt Diablo Blvd & Hough Ave. Rebuilt 1935 as a 'uniquely-shaped' store and remodeled in 1949.

properties.name: Clarence Brown's Hardware
properties.description: 1930s 'Main Street' style store on the NE corner of Mt Diablo Blvd & Oak Hill Rd.

properties.name: Garrett Building
properties.description: Turreted brick building by realtor Col. N. M. Garrett, 1937.
properties.coord_source: US Census geocoder 3565 Mt Diablo Blvd

properties.name: Acalanes High School
properties.description: Opened Sept 10, 1940 with 406 students.

properties.name: Park Theater
properties.description: Opened Aug 21, 1941. Streamline Moderne with a neon marquee. Closed 2005, reopening targeted for early 2027.

properties.name: Veterans Memorial Building (WPA, demolished)
properties.description: WPA building of 1938-39 at Mt Diablo Blvd & First St. Replaced in 2005, and its site became the library.

properties.name: Hwy 24 Lafayette bypass
properties.description: The freeway through Lafayette was originally built c.1957-59 (Wilder Rd to Acalanes Rd c.1959, Acalanes Rd to I-680 c.1957) and rebuilt or reopened 1969-70. Before that, Hwy 24 ran along Mt Diablo Blvd.

properties.name: Lafayette Reservoir Recreation Area opens
properties.description: EBMUD opened it to the public June 13, 1966.

properties.name: Lafayette BART station
properties.description: Opened May 21, 1973 in the Hwy 24 median.

properties.name: Lafayette-Moraga Trail
properties.description: Rail-trail on the former Sacramento Northern right-of-way. Sources disagree on the date: opened 1974 per the LM History Trail, dedicated July 4, 1976 per EBRPD.

properties.name: Caldecott third bore
properties.description: The third bore opened Oct 1964, after the 1937 twin bores. Outside Lafayette, to the west.
